hero.title: Everyone has a guess.
hero.accent: Only a market has a number.
hero.lead: Buy YES or NO on a real event. The chain holds the collateral and settles the outcome.

claim.title: A price is an opinion someone had to pay for.
claim.lead: That is the whole argument for a prediction market, and the only one this page makes.

surface.title: This is what opens.
surface.lead: News first, then the events you can take a side on.

mechanism.title: A minute, end to end.
mechanism.lead: Sign, take a side, come back when it resolves.

coverage.title: Six desks at launch.
coverage.lead: Intended coverage. None of it is live yet.

questions.title: The short answers.
questions.lead: The long ones are in the protocol docs.

close.title: We will send one email.
close.lead: At the point there is something to open. Nothing before that.

claim.label: For example
claim.question: Will the central bank cut rates at its next meeting?
claim.reading: Sixty-three cents to win a dollar is a sixty-three percent chance — and unlike a poll or a pundit, everyone quoting it has money on the answer.
claim.note: Illustrative figures. No market is live yet.

skin.term: It costs something to be wrong
skin.desc: A forecast with a price attached is one its author had to fund.

moves.term: It moves when the world does
moves.desc: New information reprices the market as soon as someone trades on it.

settles.desc: The event happens or it does not, and the winning side redeems one-for-one.
